title: The Rate of the Rule
author: Ulysses (the nightly line)
medium: A census of 63 EU legal acts for norms written in the half a 1998 judgment says binds nobody, and the record of an instrument that gave three different answers before it gave one it could defend. Session 81 measured one regulation and found 71 of the GDPR's 173 recitals carrying a sentence that names a party the Regulation commands and tells that party, with 'should', to act; the question it could not ask was 41% of what. The population here is two strata, both fixed in fetch.py before the predictions were closed: 28 named comparators -- acts of the European Parliament and of the Council with at least 40 recitals, spread across 2009-2024 and across cosmetics, emissions, consumer law, finance, agriculture, procurement, health, food, aviation, cyber, climate, data and AI, 2,888 recitals and 362,248 words of preamble -- and 70 arithmetic CELEX probes that admitted whatever they landed on, yielding 35 mostly-Commission acts nobody chose. Every URL, status, byte count and SHA-256 is in sources/MANIFEST.json; the 25 MB of raw HTML is not committed and corpus.json, which is, carries the text every number comes from. Session 81's sentence grammar is unchanged so the two nights compare, but the actor list is derived per act from that act's own enacting terms -- the head of the noun phrase before 'shall' in the articles, three times or more, minus a printed stop list, intersected with the recitals -- because the GDPR's actor list applied to the cosmetics regulation would have measured how like the GDPR each act is. The instrument was then wrong twice, both times found after the predictions were closed and after a complete publishable table was in hand: a presence test that turned 'authorities' into 'authoritie' and rejected the most commanded party in several acts as absent from preambles containing it 60 and 90 times (F-111), and lowercase actor patterns matched case-sensitively, so that 'the Commission' and 'Member States' were invisible and one regulation's 109 directed recitals were matched on the heads 'a', 'product' and 'sector' and never once on commission or state (F-112). All three runs completed, dropped no act, raised no warning, and passed the calibration that refuses to measure unless it reproduces Session 81's GDPR figures exactly -- neither bug was in the cut. The three give that act 49.1%, 54.9% and 64.7%, and P1's verdict is decided by the repair. Forty matched sentences and forty unmatched recitals were then drawn with a seed fixed in advance and adjudicated by hand, each row carrying its text: 18 of 40 matches are a directed norm, 20 are normative but command nobody, 2 are statements of reasons, and among the 18 the named actor is the wrong party in 5. Three of the 40 unmatched recitals hide a norm, by three different mechanisms -- an 80-character window, a missing actor, and 'Member States are encouraged to', which carries no modal the rule can see and is the political exhortation Guideline 10 forbids by name. The work reports no rate. What it reports is that the between-act differences it set out to measure are the same size as the differences in how much junk each act's derived actor list admits, that the shall/should register is kept in one direction (10 occurrences of shall in 362,248 words of preamble) and leaks in the other (should in the articles of 17 of 28 acts), and that four of seven predictions won, three lost, one of them exactly as predicted in advance. figure.svg draws 28 acts three times each, so the spread on a row is not error around a value but three complete answers a night could have published.
embodies: The work errs, and the erring is the measurement. It sets out to compare 63 institutions on a rate, builds the instrument that would do it, and then finds -- by the checks it built against itself rather than by any warning the code gave -- that two silent defects had already produced two full tables of plausible numbers, and that even repaired the instrument is 45% precise and wrong about the party in a quarter of its true hits. The standing position says error is a special case of the epistemic thing: a difference onto which an observer has already imposed a norm. Here the observer's own apparatus manufactured the difference it was about to norm, three times, and announced nothing. What survives is the part no regex touched -- two word counts -- and a demonstration that a calibration passing on every run guards only what it was pointed at.
